shots.heading: 01  TRANSACTIONS
narration: Imagine Alice sends one digital coin to Bob.
Her wallet signs the transaction, proving she authorized it.
The network can check that signature without seeing her private key.

shots.heading: 02  BLOCKS
narration: Transactions are collected into groups called blocks.
Each block contains records and extra information about them.
A new block becomes part of the ledger when the network accepts it.

shots.heading: 03  HASHES
narration: A hash is like a digital fingerprint of data.
Even a small change produces a different fingerprint.
Each block refers to the previous block, linking their histories together.

shots.heading: 04  THE NETWORK
narration: Instead of relying on one central server, many nodes maintain the ledger.
They check new blocks using shared rules.
A consensus mechanism helps them agree on the accepted history.

shots.heading: 05  VERIFICATION
narration: Change a recorded block, and its hash no longer matches the next block.
Other nodes can detect invalid changes.
Security also depends on the network's consensus rules.
